findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled()
findings.body: update() loads the pre-update IDP with getById(), which, when the ORGANIZATION feature is on, returns a wrapper whose isEnabled() is false if the linked organization is missing or disabled, even when the IDP row itself is enabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), whose ENABLED check calls that overridden isEnabled(). If the org is disabled, the original model fails the predicate, and the method returns immediately whenever the updated model also fails it (hide-on-login, link-only, not broker-public, or disabled) without comparing organizationId. The getForLogin cache was filled from the JPA delegate using the raw columns, so that IDP id stays in the cached list. Later getForLogin replays the cached ids and returns an IDP that no longer matches the login filters. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login, link-only, or broker-public. After the organization is enabled again, the login page can show brokers the admin hid, marked link-only, or made non-public until the realm cache entry is evicted. Decide invalidation from the unwrapped delegate model (raw isEnabled/isHideOnLogin/isLinkOnly/config and organizationId), not the organization-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Per-org login lookups evict the shared FetchMode cache
findings.body: getForLogin stores every organizationId under one realm+FetchMode entry (search key is the org id, cache key is only realm and mode). The login UI calls getForLogin(ALL, orgId) once per organization. The first org fills the entry; each new org misses its search key and calls cache.invalidateObject on that shared key before merging a replacement. That evicts every organization's cached login-IDP list for the mode, including on other cluster nodes, on a read path. Concurrent logins for different orgs also lose merged search keys: each request merges only its own key into the old snapshot and the last addRevisioned wins. In a multi-organization realm the cache never stays warm and the login page keeps hitting the database. Put organizationId in the cache key (with a dedicated key for null) so a lookup does not invalidate other organizations.

findings.title: Login-cache test cleans up the wrong IDP alias
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias") (the literal string) both in the create loop and again for idp-alias-20, instead of the alias just created. The admin client get() returns a resource proxy, so this does not remove idp-alias-0..20. Teardown can 404, and those providers stay in the shared test realm. The same literal is already used in testCacheIDPByOrg. Leftover enabled or public brokers change later getForLogin counts and can fail this class or later organization tests. Register cleanup with the actual alias (get(alias) and get("idp-alias-20")).
